headline: New Mexico Reaches 2030 Renewable Goal Six Years Early
meta_description: New Mexico hit its 2030 renewable energy target in 2024, reaching 50% renewable electricity six years ahead of schedule.
summary_short: New Mexico achieved its 2030 renewable energy milestone six years early, with the state generating 50% renewable electricity in 2024.
body:
New Mexico has reached its 2030 renewable energy target six years ahead of schedule, hitting 50% renewable electricity in 2024. The achievement signals how quickly clean energy infrastructure can scale when policy and investment align.

The state's largest utility pushed even further, generating 80% carbon-free power in 2025 as New Mexico continues expanding wind and solar installations. This rapid progress demonstrates that ambitious climate goals, once considered far-off aspirations, can materialize far sooner than expected.

The early milestone reflects years of investment in wind farms and solar arrays across the state, transforming New Mexico's energy landscape and positioning it as a leader in the nation's transition to cleaner power.
quick_facts: New Mexico reached 50% renewable electricity in 2024
Achievement came six years ahead of 2030 target
State's largest utility generated 80% carbon-free power in 2025
Expansion driven by wind and solar development
